newsitem.title: UK: Lower gold price, charge hit Ashanti profit.
newsitem.headline: Lower gold price, charge hit Ashanti profit.

text.p: Ghana's Ashanti Goldfields Co Ltd on Tuesday reported a 42.5 percent fall in second quarter earnings, which were hit by an exceptional charge and a lower gold price.
But the company, which is West Africa's largest gold miner, said it was on track to meet 1997 production and cost forecasts.
Earnings fell to $7.7 million after a $2.5 million charge for redundancy costs, which compares with earnings of $13.4 million a year ago.
Ashanti realised a gold price of $450 per ounce, down from $465 in the second quarter of 1996.
The company said it has over five million ounces hedged at a price of over $420 per ounce.
"Ashanti is well protected against the current low gold price and the core capital expenditure programmes at Obuasi, Bibiani and Siguiri are continuing on track," it said.

The Ghanaian Obuasi mine is Ashanti's main producing asset. Bibiani and Siguiri are the group's main exploration projects in respectively Ghana and Guinea. Construction at both projects is going according to plan.
Ashanti, which has a total of 35 exploration projects in 12 African countries, cut its Obuasi workforce by 800 or eight percent in a move to reduce its cost base.
The related $2.5 million charge will have paid itself back after 18 months, the group expects
Ashanti sees production growth in the second half of the year and said it remains confident that the 1997 objective to produce 1.1 million ounces at $265 per pounce will be met.
"During the rest of 1997 the group will continue its focus on reducing operating costs, particularly at Obuasi and on developing Bibiani and Siguiri," Ashanti said.
The group left its interim dividend unchanged at $0.125 per share.
